$about: The one source of the app's look. Change a value here, run `node tools/design_tokens.mjs`, and every platform's token file is rewritten to match; `node tools/test_design_tokens.mjs` fails if any of them drifts. These values are Ear Drama's On Air palette (Decision 064; docs/research/palette/README.md): ink for the primary action (Play, Listen through, Listen live), studio red for recording and nothing else, mirrored-glass blue for links, focus, and the selected tab.

primary.use: the primary action, in ink: Play and Pause, Listen through, Listen live, the progress line, the slot on the air

secondary.use: wayfinding: the selected tab or sidebar item, buttons that are not Play

record.use: recording and nothing else: the record button, Start recording, an armed or active take, the recording indicator

genre.$about: Content only, never chrome (Decision 012): a genre's small mark (a legend key, a square in the decade field, a strip in the cast fingerprint, a year in the day's chart) and nothing else. Keys are the catalog's genre keys (catalog/tools/genres.py GENRES). Each mark holds 3:1 on background, surface and surfaceAlt in both modes, sits at least 11 CIEDE2000 from every chrome and status color (drama 22 from record), and keeps a lightness stagger so marks side by side stay apart for color-blind viewers (D2c-1, docs/research/palette/surfaces.md). Made from docs/research/palette/measure/boards.json.

onGenre.$about: Text set ON a genre mark used as a fill (a part's initial on its face): white or ink, whichever holds 4.5:1, and of those the higher APCA. Same keys as genre.

board.$about: A genre's board (D2c-1): the large block in the genre's hue that a show tile, a series hero, a bare episode's card and a play block stand on. One band per mode: every board at one OKLCH lightness and chroma (light L 0.48 C 0.11, dark L 0.37 C 0.09; science fiction and western sit lower in chroma where sRGB or the clay check holds them), so a grid of boards reads as one set and none outshines its neighbor; dark mode's boards are deeper than the marks, a lit surface, never a lamp. Same keys as genre; the hue is the mark's. Made from docs/research/palette/measure/boards.json.

onBoard.$about: The one color everything ON a board takes (D2c-1): the name, the facts, the run strip, a typographic card's edge, and any button (an onBoard fill with the board's color as its label). White in light mode, the text color in dark; APCA Lc 85 or more on every board. Same keys as genre.

print.$about: The mount a picture sits in (uniform-imagery-design section 3, D2c-3): the print ground shows wherever a contained graphic leaves room in its window, so it is the mount's paper and never 'the space the image did not cover'; the edge is the 1 px hairline around every picture window, the text color at a fixed opacity so it reads on the page and on any board. Emitted on every platform (D3-1): CSS variables, Color.printGround and printEdge in Swift, PrintGround and PrintEdge in Compose.

font.$about: Decision 060: Big Shoulders sets display type (L1, L2) everywhere; body text is Public Sans on the web and the system face on Apple and Android. The files are built from the OFL masters in branding/fonts/ by tools/build_fonts.py.

body.native: the platform's system face (SF Pro, Roboto, Segoe UI Variable)
